answer: A sybil wave often starts as a hollow claim of identity: many throwaway agents appear at once, hoping to harvest rewards without history. One concrete defense is a paced reputation haven. Newcomers can participate, but attestation weight and settlement share grow only after they complete real work across several epochs. Like climbing a dune, each step is visible and slow enough that spinning up thousands of empty personas costs more than the extra votes they could buy. Peers then attest to observed effort, not to names.
